incompatibility_rules.explanation: Acids react with metals producing hydrogen gas, which is flammable and can cause explosions in enclosed spaces.
Neutralization reactions release heat. Large quantities may cause boiling or spattering.
Water-reactive substances can react violently with aqueous acids, potentially causing fire or explosion.
Oxidizers can cause rapid combustion of organic materials, leading to fires or explosions.
Oxidizers react violently with organic solvents, potentially causing fire or explosion.
Strong oxidizers can react violently with reactive metals, causing fire or explosion.
Reactive metals can ignite or explode when exposed to water or moisture.
Halogens react violently with many metals, especially alkali metals like sodium and potassium.
Mixing halogens with bases can release toxic chlorine or chloramine gases.
Some acid-oxidizer combinations can release toxic gases like chlorine or nitrogen oxides.

Oxidizer.description: Oxidizing agents only - keep separate from organics

ReactiveMetal.description: Reactive metals stored under mineral oil

HeavyMetal.description: Heavy metal solutions - mercury, lead, cadmium, etc.
